'''Drucker stability''' (also called the '''Drucker stability postulates''') refers to a set of mathematical criteria that restrict the possible nonlinear [[cauchy stress tensor|stress]]-[[infinitesimal strain theory|strain]] relations that can be satisfied by a solid material.<ref>{{Citation|last=Drucker|first=D.C.|title=A definition of a stable inelastic material|year=1959|journal=Journal of Applied Mechanics|volume=26|issue=1 |pages=101–195|doi=10.1115/1.4011929 |bibcode=1959JAM....26..101D }}</ref>  The postulates are named after [[Daniel C. Drucker]]. A material that does not satisfy these criteria is often found to be [[Elastic instability|unstable]] in the sense that application of a load to a material point can lead to arbitrary [[deformation (mechanics)|deformation]]s at that material point unless an additional length or time scale is specified in the [[constitutive relations]].

The Drucker stability postulates are often invoked in nonlinear [[finite element analysis]].  Materials that satisfy these criteria are generally well-suited for numerical analysis, while materials that fail to satisfy this criterion are likely to present difficulties (i.e. non-uniqueness or singularity) during the solution process.

== Drucker's first stability criterion ==
Drucker's first stability criterion (first proposed by [[Rodney Hill]] and also called '''Hill's stability criterion'''<ref>{{Citation|last=Hill|first=R.|year=1958|title=  general theory of uniqueness and stability in elastic-plastic solids|journal=Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids|volume=6|issue=3|pages=236–249|doi=10.1016/0022-5096(58)90029-2|bibcode=1958JMPSo...6..236H}}</ref>) is a strong condition on the incremental internal energy of a material which states that the incremental internal energy can only increase.  The criterion may be written as follows:
:<math>
   \text{d}\boldsymbol{\sigma}:\text{d}\boldsymbol{\varepsilon} \ge 0
 </math>,
where d'''σ''' is the stress increment tensor associated with the strain increment tensor d'''ε''' through the constitutive relation.

== Drucker's stability postulate ==
Drucker's postulate is applicable to elastic-plastic materials and states that in a cycle of [[plasticity (physics)|plastic]] deformation the second degree plastic work is always positive.  This postulate can be expressed in incremental form as
:<math>
   \text{d}\boldsymbol{\sigma}:\text{d}\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_p \ge 0 
 </math>,
where d'''ε'''<sub>p</sub> is the incremental plastic strain tensor.
